name: Standing Calf Stretch
summary: A static lower-leg stretch performed in a staggered stance, targeting the gastrocnemius and Achilles tendon.

setup: Stand facing a wall or sturdy support roughly arm's length away.
Place your hands on the wall at shoulder height for support.
Step one leg straight back into a staggered stance, keeping both feet pointed directly forward.
steps: Keep the rear leg completely straight with the heel pressed firmly flat into the floor.
Bend your front knee and gently shift your hips forward until you feel a moderate stretch in the upper calf of the back leg.
Hold the position steadily without bouncing for the desired duration, then switch legs.
instructions.breathing: Breathe smoothly and deeply throughout the hold, relaxing into the stretch on each exhale.
cues: Drive the back heel into the floor

common_faults.fault: Allowing the back heel to lift off the ground.
common_faults.correction: Shorten your stance slightly so the rear heel remains firmly anchored to the floor.
Keep both feet aligned pointing straight ahead to target the calf evenly.
Keep the back knee fully extended to place the stretch primarily on the gastrocnemius.

precautions: Stretch to a point of gentle tension, not sharp pain.
